object: generic birthday, 7-lane SWAR rho/DP, m8..m15 chain
question: What does plain birthday cost on the complete 3-round BLAKE3-256 under collision-frontier-v5 with C=638?
number: time_log2 = 125.134 (q = 0.9943*2^128 evaluations, 88.0 word ops per evaluation / 638); memory < 2^20 bytes; score 125.134
evidence: research/blake3_r3/swar_count.py (lanes checked against verifier/blake3.py on 64-byte messages, 0 mismatches); research/blake3_r3/ANALYSIS.md
notes: gain is against the nominal 2^128 (one unit per evaluation). Program not yet written as a filed package; DP test 4 ops per batch assumed; registers assumed free for 40 words.

object: 2-round line (55/63 length cancel, D={4,5}) extended by round 2
question: How many 32-bit checks remain in the digest after a third round?
number: word-level model (each message-difference word silences up to 2 outputs of its call; calibrated: r1=0 and r2=4 = four-checks theorem). For message-difference sets of size <= 3: r2 4 checks, r3 6 checks at best; for the 2-round line's own D={4,5}: r3 8 checks (all 256 bits). For |D|>=4 the model is vacuous (it gives 0 even at r2)
evidence: research/blake3_r3/act2.cpp, act4.cpp; outputs quoted in ANALYSIS.md
notes: model is generous to the attacker (no solvability check) and is NOT a bound for |D|>=4 (local-collision routes, priced separately at about 2^65 for r2 in sol_answer_D4_local.md, GUESS there). For |D|<=3 six or more checks x 32 bits: the 2-round gain of about 68 bits over its own plain birthday (124.98 -> 57.0) only ties plain birthday at 6 checks.

question: Is any message-difference set closed under the G-call pairings of all three rounds?
number: after 2 rounds the pair-closed sets are {0,1,2,3,6,7,10,11}, {4,5,12,13}, {8,9,14,15}; after 3 rounds only the full 16-word set
evidence: ANALYSIS.md section 3 (union-find on the PERMUTATION of verifier/blake3.py)

question: Does the genuine 256-bit chain (identity embedding in m8..m15) behave like a random mapping on n-bit tags?
notes: supports the random-mapping premise of the generic line at small widths only. A one-word embedding (rho_check.c) gave 0.68 at n=32 and is NOT the real chain; do not cite it for the premise.

object: chaining-value difference + free final block (near-collision first block, then semi-free-start)
question: Does a 224-bit near-collision of first blocks plus a free final block beat 2^125?
number: stage A alone: 2^112 evaluations x 0.14 = 2^109.1; stage B (one differing chaining-value word, free blocks): word-level model gives 8 checks unless pins exist, i.e. generic 2^128
notes: stage B has no pin: a cancelled difference in K0 leaves a single message-difference word whose later uses (C2, H1) activate every diagonal. Untested by search.
